newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Aerolineas and Iberia meet Argentine econ minister.
newsitem.headline: Aerolineas and Iberia meet Argentine econ minister.

text.p: The chiefs of Aerolineas Argentinas and Spanish carrier Iberia met Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez Thursday to tell him of plans for cooperation on routes and tickets with other airlines.
An Economy Ministry official said the meeting included Spanish Deputy Industry Minister Pedro Ferraras, Iberia chief Xabier de Irala and Aerolineas President Manuel Moran.
"They are looking for complementary arrangements with American Airlines and British Airways," said the official.

He confirmed that Iberia did not have plans to sell its stake in Aerolineas. This commitment was expressed earlier this week by Spain's Industry and Energy Minister Josep Pique Camps, who said his government interested instead in "seeking alliances to boost commercially" Aerolineas and Iberia.
The Spanish government owns about 45 percent of Aerolineas through a direct 20 percent stake held by state-owned Iberia Lineas Aereas de Espana SA and another stake in a holding company.
There has been speculation that Aerolineas is about to enter into an alliance with American Airlines which could involve route swaps or sales.

The Argentine Economy Ministry official said the airline chiefs had explained that "Iberia is not pulling out of its share in Aerolineas but seeking a complementary deal on routes to work with these two companies. They also want to establish ticket-sharing," he said.
